page: Amazon Web Services r7i.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 8488C processors operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz, configured with 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs. The processor setup includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 105 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for vector and matrix acceleration instructions such as AVX-512, AMX-Tile, and AMX-INT8, alongside cryptographic hardware extensions.

The instance delivers 128.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a generous 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local NVMe instance storage is absent, requiring reliance on network-attached storage architectures. Networking bandwidth provides a baseline speed of 6 Gbps. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs, relying on CPU extensions like AMX and AVX-512 for accelerated compute tasks.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core and compression performance. In Geekbench testing, the instance scored 2141.0 in single-core evaluation and 2740.0 in text processing, both placing in the top quartile. Single-threaded compression workflows demonstrated high throughput, achieving 33.78 GB/sec in gzip compression and 13.9 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Small-model LLM generation yielded strong results at 333.12 tokens per second. Multi-core compute and throughput benchmarks remain consistent in mid-tier percentiles, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 26176.98, multi-core stress-ng score of 15858.69, and Redis SET throughput of 21.24 million operations per second.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the r7i.4xlarge provides dense DDR5 memory capacity per core without the added expense of attached local solid-state drives or GPU hardware. The absence of local disk implies dependencies on external storage systems, which shapes storage design trade-offs. The configuration is primarily suitable for in-memory caching solutions like Redis, relational database systems, in-memory analytics, and enterprise applications requiring high memory-to-vCPU footprints.
